# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (Brian Flynn mystery novels, 1920s, Gutenberg texts)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Case of the Black Twenty-Two" (Gutenberg 75209; Grosset & Dunlap, 1929)

**Chapter list:** I Mr. Daventry Receives a Commission; II Schedule Numbers 37, 38 and 39; III The Hanover Galleries Murder; IV Peter Daventry Is Mindful of Mr. Bathurst; V The Assynton Lodge Murder; VI Marjorie Lennox Doesn't Mince Matters; VII Butterworth Is Apprehensive of the Future; VIII The 6:55 Carries a Trio of Distinction; IX Mr. Bathurst Opens His Bedroom Door; X The Incident of the Boot-Boy's Bicycle; XI With a Given Center, Mr. Bathurst Describes a Circle; XII The Second Screen of Mary Stuart; XIII Colonel Leach-Fletcher Is at Home to Visitors; XIV Mr. Bathurst Takes a Book from the Bookcase; XV Mr. Daventry Gets His Feet Wet; XVI Mr. Bathurst Again Samples the Bookcase; XVII The Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure; XVIII The Room at Blanchard's Hotel; XIX Inspector Goodall Is Entertained; XX Mr. Bathurst Brushes Up His History; XXI Mr. Ferguson of New York; XXII Mr. Bathurst Baits the Hook; XXIII When the Cat's Away; XXIV The Secret of the Screens; XXV The Riddle of the Black Twenty-Two.

**Characters:**
- Peter Daventry: junior partner, firm "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry, Solicitors", Cornhill. Brother Gerald Daventry (accountant, Wedderburn and Rathbone, Devonshire Place; M.C.C. member).
- David Linnell: senior partner, 58, from Lancashire.
- Plunkett: 35-yr clerk. Collins: office messenger.
- Laurence P. Stewart: American millionaire, Assynton Lodge, Berkshire (near Wantage); collector obsessed with Mary Queen of Scots; believed descendant. Murdered (skull battered, 3 blows) in library, found by son's household at morning; revolver in left dressing-gown pocket, one chamber discharged.
- Charles Stewart: son, ~22, tennis that evening; cousin-like "so-called cousin" to Marjorie.
- Marjorie Lennox: ward, auburn/blue-eyed, retroussé nose; lace handkerchief with "M. L." found by Clegg in curtains.
- Morgan Llewellyn: secretary, early 30s, pince-nez, reddish-brown eyes; "M. L."; love letter to Marjorie.
- John Butterworth: butler, 60+, ex-service of Sir Julian Kennedy; wife housekeeper (married 37 years); killer.
- Colonel Leach-Fletcher: neighbour, dined with Stewart; drove off ~10 pm; Renan's *Vie de Jésus* on desk.
- Anthony Bathurst: amateur sleuth, Oxford-era acquaintance of Gerald; "Cheerio"; grey eyes; Considine Manor affair reference.
- Detective-Inspector Goodall: Scotland Yard, stoutish, blue serge suit.
- Sergeant Clegg (Amos): Assynton local; wife 17 years; "By Gum".
- P.C. Potter. Druce (night watchman, 60; 6 years service). Jim Mason (murdered watchman at Hanover Galleries). Mrs. Turner (cleaner). Ronald Forshaw (young Forshaw). Day (Day, Forshaw and Palmers auctioneers), Palmers.
- Patrick O'Connor (boot-boy, 18; bicycle). Michael O'Connor (father, foundryman, black beard).
- Maidment (gardener). Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter (maids). Mrs. Briggs (cook).
- Marriott (lunch companion at Violette). Gustave (waiter).
- Ferguson (Andrew Ferguson, of Crake and Ferguson, NY solicitors).
- Alice Mortimer (Butterworth's daughter, née Butterworth) and "Snoop" Mortimer / "Flash Alf" (NY crook, arrested). Lal? none in book 1.

**Key events in order:**
1. Peter at Cornhill; Linnell receives letter (June 7, Assynton Lodge) commissioning purchase at Day, Forshaw and Palmers' sale (June 10, Hanover Galleries, W.1) of Schedule Nos. 37 "Collar of Pearls", 38 "Antique Tapestry Fire-screen", 39 "Rosary of Amber Beads", "all ... property of Mary, Queen of Scots."
2. Lunch at the Violette; Peter says aloud "So's Mary, Queen of Scots!" after Marriott's "Queen Anne's dead"; man at next table knocks cruet to floor; woman's warning look; overheard "let's go to-morrow—not to-day."
3. Peter views items; screen text in beads: "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"; corners Royal Lion, fleur-de-lis, Leopards and Lilies. Two plain-clothes men watch.
4. Telegrams from Stewart: "Say! What the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy. Got that? Stewart." and "Say—you don't look before you leap—you take a magnifying glass. Same name as before."
5. Day morning: Mason murdered, three items stolen; watchman Druce; woman decoy asked way to Marble Arch, "sneezed several times"; key missing; office door unlocked.
6. Stewart murdered night before in library; Charles phones Peter. Peter recommends Bathurst (Gerald → Princes club, Leyton/Middlesex–Essex match).
7. Assynton: Clegg finds handkerchief; Llewellyn lies about times; Marjorie accuses Llewellyn, storms off; Butterworth heard Stewart and Marjorie ~10:10.
8. Bathurst 6:55 train with Goodall; Clegg meets them at station. Bicycle with tar-marked tyres (Patrick). Tests: ink-bowl dirt; coal-scuttle pebbles; Museum Room catalogue (2,044 items); missing fire-screen (No. 866 in catalogue).
9. Marjorie describes second screen: "Timeo Danaos", big fish in centre, Lion, Leopards, Lilies. Blanchard's Hotel call (11 min, Clifford St); Mr & Mrs Laurence Charles Stewart (from NY).
10. Colonel Leach-Fletcher: Stewart upset over treachery and son's conduct; book on desk. Llewellyn love letter found in Renan (Peter finds it).
11. Bathurst reconstructs: Butterworth killed Stewart; stone path-piece used as weapon, thrown in pool (Peter wades); shot fired from Stewart into bookcase's *Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure* (848 pages).
12. Memoirs passage: "Black Twenty-Two"; Girardier made two screens; ink-bowl stone; Blanchard's hotel room: hay-fever smell, black glasses, Atkins/Rabjohns evidence.
13. Ferguson of NY arrives; will: £250,000 to Marjorie, residue to Charles, conditions (marry each other). Butterworth £500 p.a.; Llewellyn £300 annuity.
14. Bathurst sends servants away; night raid at Assynton; Snoop Mortimer & Alice Mortimer arrested for Mason murder; Butterworth arrested for Stewart murder. Screen: fish-eye pressed → cavity → 22 black pearls ("Black Pearls of Lorraine"). ICHTHUS explanation (Greek initials of "Iesous Christos Theos Soter").
15. Bathurst: Stewart to marry Rosemary Armitage (The Towers); Marjorie to be given pearls.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Mystery of the Peacock's Eye" (Gutenberg 75195; John Hamilton Ltd, London, 1928)

**Chapter list:** I The Hunt Ball at Westhampton; II Mr. Bathurst Receives a Distinguished Visitor; III Chief-Inspector Bannister Gets a "Busman's Holiday"; IV A Case of Identity; V John Martin's Evidence; VI Mr. Bathurst Changes His Destination; VII Gentlemen and Players; VIII Daphne Draws Up the Blinds; IX Mr. Bathurst Looks at a Pair of Shoes—and a Luggage-Wagon; X A Room Is Ransacked at "Rest Harrow"; XI A Newspaper and a Second Suit-Case; XII Mr. Bathurst Listens to a Little Local Gossip; XIII Re-enter Mr. X; XIV The Peacock's Eye; XV Alan Warburton Leads Trumps; XVI Of Which Mr. Bathurst Holds the Ace; XVII Bannister Strikes the Trail; XVIII That Leads Round the Mulberry-Bush; XIX Ronald Branston's Story; XX "Findings—Keepings"; XXI The Lord Lieutenant Goes Back a Few Years; XXII Gallant Mr. Bathurst; XXIII Mr. Bathurst Forgets His Change; XXIV What Did Mr. Bathurst Whisper?; XXV Mr. Bathurst's Patience Is Rewarded; XXVI Rendezvous; XXVII Sir Austin Kemble Removes His Hat.

**Characters:**
- Sheila Delaney: auburn-haired beauty, daughter of late Colonel Daniel "Dan" Delaney (drowned at Nillebrook Water, 1917, Gallipoli leave); mother d. ~4 yrs before; lives at "Rest Harrow", Tranfield (near Westhampton). Murdered.
- "Pinkie" (Agnes Kerr): old nurse-companion, home Otterton, Devon (4 Rolle Cottages); postcard "Dear Miss Sheila… Much love from 'Pinkie'".
- Major Desmond Carruthers: Chief Constable of Westhamptonshire; killed in motor accident (March, previous year, wet night, overturned); friend of Delaney; Daphne's uncle.
- Daphne Carruthers: niece; 11 Lexham Gardens, Kensington; flat; staying at Cassandra, Seabourne; photo with Crown Prince.
- Crown Prince Alexis of Clorania ("Mr. Lucius" incognito); marrying Princess Imogena of Natalia in December; blackmailed by letters (five; first dated April 23 Tranfield post-mark, last June 22 Westhampton).
- Alan Warburton: nephew of Sir Felix Warburton (Mutual Bank frauds; arrested; suicide in cell); 19 Crossley Road, Westhampton; blackmailer; wrote letters; Sheila's ex-lover.
- Captain Willoughby: at Cassandra; fiancé of Lois Travers (Crowborough Mansions, Maida Vale); bought stolen notes' origin (racing win at Newmarket, horse "Sherlock Holmes"); bookmaker Jacob Morley, 9 Macbeth Court Mansions.
- Chief-Inspector Richard "Dandy Dick" Bannister: Scotland Yard, horn-rimmed glasses; killer; retires after.
- Sergeant Godfrey (Marlshire County Police, Seabourne); P.C. Stannard, P.C. Waghorn; Doctor Renfrew (divisional surgeon); Mrs. Pearson (searcher).
- Ronald Branston: dentist, Coolwater Avenue corner, Seabourne; housekeeper Mrs. Bertenshaw (son in Calcutta; £50 loan repaid).
- Martin (reception clerk, Lauderdale Hotel), Maynard (manager), Falcon (Grand Hotel, Westhampton).
- E. Kingsley Stark: Manager, Mutual Bank Westhampton; cashier Churchill; gave note numbers; "Peacock's Eye" deposit.
- Sir Matthew Fullgarney (Lord Lieutenant; Dovaston Court); Lady Pauline Fullgarney.
- Lal Singh: fake Indian (Ram Das passenger alias); actually Bannister in disguise (beard gummed on).
- Sir Austin Kemble: Commissioner; Brigadier-General.
- Rogers and Davidson: commercial travellers; saw Warburton.
- Ross: Westhampton/Tranfield Sergeant.
- Cuypers: Dutch police head, Amsterdam. Stefanopoulos (Demetri): Greek "fence", Jewish quarter.
- Lady Brantwood (Brantwood Castle).
- Hotels: Florizel (London), Cassandra (Seabourne), Lauderdale (Seabourne), Grand Hotel (Westhampton), Red Dolphin.

**Key events in order:**
1. Hunt Ball, Westhampton (Feb, prior year); Carruthers with unnamed "Mr. X" (Bannister); Sheila dances with "Mr. X"; Sir Felix Warburton suicide same day as ball; Carruthers killed in March later.
2. Crown Prince visits Bathurst (letter from Hotel Florizel); blackmail letters; Bathurst takes case. Crown Prince claims Sheila was not met at ball.
3. Bannister at Seabourne holiday; Sergeant Godfrey calls him; Branston's surgery; Sheila dead in chair, prussic acid (hydrocyanic) by syringe; Branston locked in work-room with brass bolt.
4. Hand-bag/labels: Daphne Carruthers name tags on Sheila's case booked at Lauderdale by phone Wed 10:50 pm; Martin identifies Sheila.
5. Crown Prince's Daphne phone call reveals Daphne alive; Daphne identifies Sheila at mortuary; Willoughby confirms not Lois Travers.
6. Bannister at Tranfield "Rest Harrow"; ransacked bedroom; keys; hand-bag with Warburton card (Branston address on back); Standard car in garage; Seabourne Herald newspaper in car; second suit-case under seat.
7. Stark's note-numbers; three stolen notes traced to Willoughby → Morley → Branston → Mrs. Bertenshaw (found notes in art-pot).
8. Warburton confesses to Bathurst, "Alan Warburton" blackmail; Bathurst reconstructs; Lal Singh's "Hindustani" wrong dialect.
9. Bathurst meets Sir Matthew: Peacock's Eye story — 44 years ago, Baluchistan, Sacred Peacock temple near Bolan Pass; Delaney won stone by lot; Lal Singh was servant.
10. Amsterdam trap (Café Suisse, Kalverstraat; Stefanopoulos shop); Lal Singh (Bannister disguised) arrested for Sheila's murder. Bathurst's reveal: killer's name is Sir Matthew Fullgarney? (Final line: Bathurst whispered "Yours, Sir Matthew!" — this is the joke/punchline; the real murderer per narrative is Bannister.)
11. Final: Bannister is the murderer (Lal Singh/Bannister); Bathurst names "Sir Matthew" as the wrong whisper.
